suggestions.title: Unmemoized component is re-rendering excessively
suggestions.description: The static analyzer found a component without React.memo(), AND the profiler measured that 'Link' re-rendered 13 times. Without memoization, every parent render forces this component to re-render unnecessarily.

suggestions.title: React commits are exceeding 16ms budget
suggestions.description: React had 1 commit(s) that took over 16ms (the 60fps budget). The slowest was 32.7ms. This causes visible frame drops and janky animations.
suggestions.fix:
1. Use React.memo() on components that receive the same props often.
2. Use useMemo() for expensive calculations in render.
3. Use useCallback() to stabilize function references passed as props.
4. Avoid creating new objects or arrays directly in JSX.

suggestions.title: Components are re-rendering too many times
suggestions.description: The component 'Link' re-rendered 13 times during page load. This is unnecessary work that slows down the UI.
suggestions.fix:
1. Wrap 'Link' in React.memo() to skip re-renders when props haven't changed.
2. Check if the parent component is creating new object/array references on every render.
3. Use the React DevTools Profiler tab to see what triggered each re-render.

suggestions.title: Page payload is too heavy
suggestions.description: Your page downloads 5.38MB of assets. On a 3G connection this would take over 15 seconds.
suggestions.fix:
1. Enable code splitting with React.lazy().
2. Compress images and use WebP/AVIF formats.
3. Remove unused npm dependencies.
4. Audit your bundle with a tool like webpack-bundle-analyzer.

suggestions.title: Deep prop drilling detected
suggestions.description: Props are being passed through multiple component layers to reach their destination. This makes components tightly coupled and hard to refactor.
suggestions.fix: Use React Context for data that many components need (theme, user, settings). For complex state, consider Zustand or Redux Toolkit.

suggestions.title: Inline functions are causing unnecessary re-renders
suggestions.description: Inline functions were found in JSX, AND 'Link' re-rendered 13 times. Inline functions create a new reference on every render, which breaks React.memo() and triggers child re-renders.

suggestions.title: Missing memoization is slowing React commits
suggestions.description: Components are missing React.memo(), AND React commits are averaging 32.7ms — above the 16ms 60fps budget. Without memoization, React re-renders everything on every update.
suggestions.fix: Add React.memo() to pure functional components that receive stable props. Also review useMemo() for expensive computations inside render.

suggestions.title: Prop drilling is causing cascade re-renders
suggestions.description: Deep prop drilling was detected in the code, AND components are re-rendering 13 times. When a top-level prop changes, every component in the drilling chain re-renders.
suggestions.fix: Replace prop drilling with React Context or a state management library (Zustand). This breaks the re-render cascade by letting only subscribed components update.

suggestions.title: Inline styles in components
suggestions.description: Components are using inline style objects. Every render creates a new object reference, which prevents React from skipping re-renders even when nothing visually changed.
suggestions.fix: Move styles to a CSS file, CSS module, or define them outside the component so the reference stays stable between renders.

suggestions.title: Dead code found
suggestions.description: Unused variables or imports were found in your components. These add to your bundle size for no benefit.
suggestions.fix: Remove unused imports and variables. Enable ESLint's no-unused-vars rule to catch these automatically.

suggestions.title: Inline functions found in JSX props
suggestions.description: Inline arrow functions were found directly inside JSX props. Every render creates a brand new function reference, which prevents React.memo() from working correctly on child components and can trigger unnecessary re-renders.
